parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim and the objector reads it correctly: literally, (i) g≡0 and (ii) V={0,c} with both values attained do not exhaust the possibilities left by §3 (V={c} is omitted). But the omitted case is not left unproved: §7 states 'Since $S_0=\emptyset$, the function $g$ never takes the value $0$. Together with §3 this forces $g(x)\equiv c$', which is exactly the inference needed when V={c} (there S_0=∅ holds trivially, no contradiction argument required), and it yields the target f(x)=x+c. So the case is concluded, merely later than the objector would prefer; the omission is presentational and does not leave any needed statement unestablished. Hence the witness (that the case is unaddressed) fails; the defect is cosmetic and non-fatal.
